ipc_bns_mapping_note: IPC 415/417/418/419/420 <-> BNS 318/319; not 1:1. BNS 319 is specifically cheating by personation (overlaps conceptually with Digital Fraud domain).
keywords: cheating, dishonest inducement, fraudulent inducement, deception, delivery of property
inclusion_rule: Judgment substantively adjudicates the cheating charge on its merits
exclusion_rule: Section cited only in passing/background

keywords: criminal breach of trust, breach of trust, entrustment, dishonest misappropriation, conversion
inclusion_rule: Core issue is misuse of entrusted property
exclusion_rule: Incidental mention alongside unrelated charges

keywords: forgery, forged document, false document, making a false document, forged electronic record, using forged document as genuine, falsification of accounts
inclusion_rule: Forgery is the central charge, not incidental evidence
exclusion_rule: Forgery mentioned only as supporting evidence for another crime

keywords: corporate fraud, wrongful gain, company affairs, false statement, false evidence
exclusion_rule: Companies Act cited for unrelated procedural matters

keywords: money laundering, proceeds of crime, attachment, confiscation, adjudication
exclusion_rule: PMLA mentioned only in case background/citation

keywords: tax evasion, fake invoice, bogus invoice, fake/bogus invoice, input tax credit fraud, fraudulent refund, false accounts
exclusion_rule: Passing GST reference without substantive offence discussion

keywords: bribe, gratification, public servant, undue advantage
exclusion_rule: Section cited without case turning on bribery issue

keywords: undue advantage, influence, intermediary, obtaining advantage without consideration
inclusion_rule: Core issue is the act of influence/undue advantage
exclusion_rule: Incidental mention

section_for_retrieval: Sec 13 (current); Sec 13(1)(d) (historical provision; omitted w.e.f. 26 July 2018)
ipc_bns_mapping_note: Pre-26-July-2018 judgments will cite the old 13(1)(d); post-amendment judgments cite current Sec 13
keywords: criminal misconduct, disproportionate assets, illicit enrichment, misappropriation by public servant
exclusion_rule: Employment/service-law context only, no corruption charge

keywords: commercial organisation, bribing on behalf of company
exclusion_rule: Passing mention

keywords: abetment, conspiracy to bribe
inclusion_rule: Only as a supporting signal alongside a primary corruption section
exclusion_rule: Standalone generic conspiracy unrelated to corruption

keywords: identity theft, fraudulent use of credentials, password theft
exclusion_rule: Sec 66C case with no monetary component

section_for_retrieval: Sec 66D (primary); IPC 419, 420 / BNS 318, 319 (supporting, not required jointly)
ipc_bns_mapping_note: BNS 319 = cheating by personation; relevant cross-reference
keywords: online cheating, computer-based personation, cyber-enabled cheating, impersonation, cyber fraud
exclusion_rule: Personation case unrelated to money

keywords: unauthorized access, hacking, data theft, account compromise, financial loss, unauthorized transaction
exclusion_rule: Hacking/access case with no financial fraud element

section_for_retrieval: IT Act 43/66/66D + IPC 419/420 or BNS 318/319, where applicable (either, not both required)
ipc_bns_mapping_note: Independent candidate signals, not a joint requirement
keywords: UPI fraud, online payment fraud, digital wallet fraud, phishing, bank fraud online
inclusion_rule: Digital signal + financial loss + substantive adjudication
exclusion_rule: Neither signal present, or no financial element

ipc_bns_mapping_note: IPC 302 (murder) <-> BNS 103(1). IPC 120B/conspiracy deliberately excluded as a countable signal - too generic, charged alongside almost any criminal case.
keywords: murder, murdered
inclusion_rule: Murder section substantively discussed - the judgment adjudicates a murder charge/conviction/appeal
exclusion_rule: Section cited only in passing/background, or discussing an unrelated topic that happens to reference Section 302 procedurally

keywords: attempt to murder, attempted murder
exclusion_rule: Passing mention

keywords: culpable homicide not amounting to murder, culpable homicide
exclusion_rule: Passing mention

ipc_bns_mapping_note: IPC 383-389 family <-> BNS 308; not 1:1 - BNS 308 has graded sub-clauses for fear of injury, fear of death/grievous hurt, and fear of a false accusation.
keywords: extortion, extorted, protection money, hafta, blackmail, blackmailing
exclusion_rule: Extortion mentioned only within an IPC 390 robbery definition/context, not as its own charge

ipc_bns_mapping_note: IPC 364A <-> BNS 140(2). Supreme Court has held 364A/BNS 140(2) is not attracted without an actual ransom demand and threat to life - a useful natural substantiveness test.
keywords: ransom, kidnapping for ransom, demand of ransom, abduction for ransom
inclusion_rule: Ransom demand substantively established, not merely alleged
exclusion_rule: Kidnapping/abduction case with no ransom element

act: MCOCA 1999 / State Gangster Acts (UP Gangsters Act 1986, Gujarat GCTOC 2015, Karnataka KCOCA 2000) / BNS 111-112
section_for_retrieval: MCOCA Sec 3 (primary), Sec 4 (supporting); UP Gangsters Act Sec 2, 3; BNS 111, 112
ipc_bns_mapping_note: BNS 111/112 create a central organised-crime offence for the first time (in force 1 July 2024); prior prosecutions relied on state Acts like MCOCA/Gangster Acts, so pre-2024 judgments in this corpus will almost always cite the state Act, not BNS.
keywords: organised crime syndicate, continuing unlawful activity, gangster, land mafia, land grabbing, crime syndicate
exclusion_rule: Gangster Act cited for unrelated procedural matter
